author: john_masefield
text:
XXIII

THE Waiting-Place

THERE is no frigate like a book
To take us lands away,
Nor any depths of ocean roll
Too blue to dive for riches;
Ships that pass in the night,
And seek not their home port,
They have some revelation
Holy and strong,
Recovering the Paradise Lost.

With such goes my boat upon life’s solemn way,
With patient hope rides out each threatening day.

THE MIGHTY

I have been a man of many parts;
A sailor in my youth, an actor next,
And then I was a soldier at last,
But now I am a poet--and that's best!

text:
THE SECRET OF THE EARTH

I WANDERED out one summer day into a field of corn;
The sun was hot but not too hot to bear,
And I could hear the hum of bees in every ear.
Then suddenly there came from far away
A sound like thunder on the wind that blew,
But it was only some great bird flying by.
It made me think how small we are when all is said and done,
For even birds can be as big as mountains fly!

It seems to me as if all were alive!
